translation_notes: Textbook trav_existence: `if any(graph.objects(subject, pred)): return True` throws the iterator away for its truth alone, never reuses a value -- translated with the stratum's own construction, `bool(m{ {subject} {pred} ?o })`, per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 (`any(g.objects(...))` -> `bool(m{ })`); the loop over LABEL_PREDICATES and the early return are untouched (no refactoring). `{subject}`/`{pred}` are bare interpolations (both already rdflib terms, no coercion to reconsider) in the exact subject/predicate positions of INSTRUCTIONS_403's own trav_one_step example `m{ {s} p ?o }`.

LABEL_PREDICATES: RDFS.label -> rdfs:label (prefixed name); the four skos:/dc:/dcterms: URIRef(...) constants have no @prefix imported by the original file, so they stay bare IRIs (<http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#prefLabel> etc.) rather than inventing prefixes the source never declared. RDF is imported but unused in the original file too (only RDFS.label is referenced) -- kept as-is, not cleaned up.

fixture.ttl / driver.py: `_has_label(graph, subject)` takes two arguments, so the default fixture= calling convention (entry called with just the parsed graph) doesn't fit; calls= is given explicitly, one call per subject, each re-parsing fixture.ttl fresh. Five subjects: three each resolving through a different LABEL_PREDICATES member (rdfs:label, skos:altLabel, dcterms:title), one with only non-label predicates (ex:other, rdfs:comment -- the zero-solution case with real neighbouring data), one absent from the graph entirely (zero solution, no data at all); plus a label on an unrelated subject (ex:neighbour) to prove the read is scoped to the given subject, not the whole graph.

REPAIR 2026-10-27: `bool(m{ {subject} {pred} ?o })` was NOT the same test as `any(graph.objects(subject, pred))`: `any` tests the TRUTH of the objects, so a label that is "", 0, false or ""@en counts as absent in the original (and in the repository: documentation.py:48 and :54 count the classes/properties that have a label from ontologies the user supplies), present for `bool(m{ })`. Proved by the strengthened driver (FAIL call[7..10] with `bool`, OK with the fix). Translation is now `if any(m{ {subject} {pred} ?o }):`, which keeps rdflib's truthiness exactly; the `any` stays Python, only the iterator is replaced.

repair.driver: fixture gets the two LABEL_PREDICATES members no subject used (skos:prefLabel, dc:title), the falsy labels ("", 0, false, ""@en), a falsy label next to a truthy one (same predicate, or another predicate), truthy non-string objects (IRI, blank node, number); driver adds 12 calls (17 in all) incl. the neighbour that carries a label of its own; docstring says what each exercises.
repair.remaining: Classification: the pair is now `any(m{ ... })` against `any(graph.objects(...))`; for Maxime to judge whether trav_existence is still credited as `bool(m{ })` (no: the construction is m{ } consumed by Python's any) and whether the pair keeps directly-expressible (the call is longer than the original, the gain is nil or negative in tokens).

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the loop with its early returns becomes `return any(any(graph.objects(subject, pred)) for pred in LABEL_PREDICATES)` (same short circuit, same truth test on the objects, a bool returned).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `any(m{ {subject} {pred} ?o }(graph))` in place of `any(graph.objects(subject, pred))`, with the call suffix since the region is now one statement (`@graph graph` measures the same). The inner `any` keeps rdflib's truthiness of the labels, as the translation's repair requires.
No exception to the symmetry rule. Folding the loop over LABEL_PREDICATES into one `{subject} ?p ?o` match filtered in Python would be longer on both sides.
header_optimization_notes: Python: RDF goes from the rdflib import.
LD Python: RDF and RDFS go from the rdflib import; the rdf: @prefix line goes, rdfs: stays (LABEL_PREDICATES writes rdfs:label).
